README.md.text:
# Fog of War chess bot

An observation-only Python engine for the [MIT 6.7980 challenge](https://www.mit.edu/~6.7980/fow/).

**V5: 261 wins, 8 draws, 131 losses against released v2 in 400 fresh
games (66.25% score), with zero failures and every replay audited.** It passed
the preregistered comparison gate. Separate regression controls scored 59 wins
and one loss in 60 games. All 188 Python tests, two static package checks and
both complete games using the extracted submission launcher passed.

The candidate uses a 600 ms internal ceiling versus v2's 180 ms, under identical
180+2 game clocks. This is a shared-host local comparison. The multiplicity-adjusted
bounded-pair interval is 55.31%–77.19%, conditional on independent pair outcomes;
shared host load can violate that assumption. The result does not isolate
algorithmic improvement from extra computation.

**MIT arena Elo remains unmeasured.** The 2200–2500 target requires actual rated
arena games. No arena account, submission or activation has been used.

See the [V5 experiment and research rationale](analysis/optimization-v5.md),
[validation report](outputs/validation-v5.md),
[tested submission ZIP](outputs/submission-v5-final.zip),
[frozen plan](outputs/v5-cycle-20261113/wave-001/plan.json) and
[complete final suite](outputs/v5-cycle-20261113/wave-001/final-learned_600/suite.json).
Earlier failures remain preserved: [v3](outputs/validation-v3.md) scored 97W/1D/102L
against v2; [v4](outputs/validation-v4.md) failed its selected-position mechanism
gate. V5 uses a separate, prospectively frozen full-game experiment.

## Run

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
source .venv/bin/activate
bash run.sh --seed 7980
```

The launcher speaks the arena stdin/stdout protocol: `fow`, color/time-control
header, `ready`, every-ply observations, and `move <uci>` after clock prompts.
Its tested defaults are:

```text
--risk-policy learned --search-ms 600 --particles 256 --worlds 6 --depth 4 --nodes 120000
```

The remaining game clock can reduce the optional-work budget. Additional CLI
arguments override defaults; altered settings require separate strength evaluation.
The raw `bot.py` entrypoint retains historical research defaults; `run.sh`
selects the validated configuration.

## Strategy

- The unchanged official tracker reconstructs exact root moves, castling rights
  and en passant from observations.
- Negative visibility identifies forced pawn blockers and impossible enemy
  placements. Occupancy evidence does not determine piece type.
- Up to 256 observation-consistent hypotheses support immediate-risk estimates;
  six sampled worlds support deeper tactical search. Recovery is explicitly
  approximate, and the bank is not a calibrated complete posterior.
- A compact bundled model supplies a soft immediate-loss signal from observation
  prefixes and known own captures. It was trained on earlier local V3 games;
  true boards supplied offline labels only. Runtime needs no NumPy.
- Bounded continuation utility and a larger loss cost prevent ordinary material
  gains from overwhelming king survival. Search still uses determinization and
  can suffer strategy fusion; it does not implement CFR or equilibrium play.
- Inference, risk scoring and search share one optional deadline. Incomplete
  comparison batches are discarded and a legal fallback remains available.

The bot receives only observations, its own moves and clock. No external engine,
network service or opponent replay truth is available during play. The
[training report](outputs/risk-model-training-v4.json) retains grouped splits,
calibration limitations and numerical warnings.

`bot_v5.py`, `belief_v5.py`, `threat_policy.py` and `fog_pressure.py` are additional
research prototypes. They are excluded from the selected launcher and submission
package; their full-game strength is unmeasured.

## Validate and package

```sh
.venv/bin/python -B -m unittest discover -v
node --test package.test.mjs
.venv/bin/python package_submission.py --output outputs/submission-new.zip
```

Use a fresh ZIP output path. The deterministic archive contains eleven
allowlisted files and stays within the 250,000-byte project payload limit.
Local environments, credentials and SoloCo state are excluded.

The V5 experiment driver freezes candidates and fresh paired seeds before play.
Its prospective guard binds the actual interpreter/dependency sources and
serializes experiment commands. Each final is 200 color-swapped pairs; at most
three attempts share a 5% error budget. At least 244 points out of 400 are needed
for its numerical gate. Failed attempts and historical reviews remain recorded.

After a passing final, separate 20-game controls against v1, the official baseline
and uniform random require 75%, 90% and 95% scores with zero failures. Those scores
are not pooled with v2 strength evidence. The package checker runs the actual
extracted launcher in both colors and audits its replays.

## Runtime and attribution

Local validation uses macOS arm64/Python 3.13.2 with chess 1.11.2 and
python-chess 1.999. The official arena documents Linux amd64/Python 3.14.8 with
4 GiB per bot. Actual arena compatibility and ratings remain unverified.

The [literature review](analysis/research-v4-literature.md) covers Obscuro,
Misty, belief recovery, information-set search and endgames. The
[arena study](analysis/research-v4-arena-evaluation.md) covers current official
rules and six reconstructed public elite replays. Sources, upstream hashes and
AI assistance are documented in [SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md).

analysis/outcome-v5-review.md.text:
# Independent V5 primary outcome review

Verified **261 wins, 8 draws and 131 losses in all 400 registered games** (200 color-swapped seed pairs). The observed score is **66.25%**. The frozen numerical gate passes: its conditional two-sided Hoeffding interval is **[0.5530983119, 0.7719016881]**, whose lower endpoint exceeds 0.5.

| Candidate color | Wins | Draws | Losses | Score |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| White | 125 | 4 | 71 | 63.5000% |
| Black | 136 | 4 | 60 | 69.0000% |
| All | 261 | 8 | 131 | 66.2500% |

The exact selected policy is `learned_600`: `--risk-policy learned --search-ms 600 --particles 256 --worlds 6 --depth 4 --nodes 120000`. It faced the byte-exact released v2 snapshot at commit `65fde033a2e65394a676e44969a992832ee17470` through `v2_bot.py --search-ms 180`, using 180+2 clocks, a 1000-ply cap and four concurrent workers. Candidate and opponent search allowances were 600 ms and 180 ms, so this was not compute-matched. The selected bot SHA256 is `0d00f07a120166821b76a04e5ef2eb991c8197701bb4392d082ebbec5d4a85e8`.

All four canonical raw batches contain 100 completed games each and match their frozen child hashes, source manifests, seed schedules, interpreter and actual white/black argument vectors. All 200 pairs contain exactly one white and one black game with matching candidate/opponent seeds. Final seeds are distinct across pairs and disjoint from development. All 24 current source bindings match the final manifest, and every archived source matches its corresponding frozen hash. No source or raw-input change was detected during review. Frozen v2 dependencies independently match their recorded snapshot manifest.

Counts and pair scores were recomputed directly from raw replay results, without trusting stored aggregates or calling the experiment driver's gate. For pair score `Xi = (white points + black points)/2` in `[0,1]`, the independent calculation uses `alpha = 0.05/3` and `radius = sqrt(log(2/alpha)/(2*200)) = 0.109401688090`. The mean is 0.6625; both the stored result and interval agree. The three-attempt allocation is a prospective family-error allowance, not evidence that outcomes are independent.

The frozen official-rule replay auditor was rerun on every raw batch. All 400 games and 28,675 plies passed complete board, observation, legal-move, terminal-result and clock reconstruction with zero recorded failures or audit errors. Its input hashes and summary agree with the saved final audit. The referee hash is `2f82ac292bfad29bcb2d701b73c060d1ca8281378b4598f08a620fe5c97255be` and validator hash is `38421d2c45ca61cd2f298f246b7fd14038e6bff680ed347bb98dfea06626f2f8`. The separate outcome/latency/diversity calculations also agree with that auditor.

From all 14,305 completed candidate moves, charged response latency was p50 = 600.898 ms, p95 = 602.756 ms, p99 = 605.278 ms, maximum = 652.933 ms. These clock deltas include local IPC and host contention; they are not CPU search times.

There are 400 distinct full UCI trajectories among 400 games, each occurring once. Opening diversity is narrower: 5 distinct four-ply prefixes, 120 eight-ply prefixes, 276 twelve-ply prefixes and 393 twenty-ply prefixes. All 200 white/black pair scores are retained in the machine summary. Distinct seeds or trajectories do not establish independence: policies, openings and host conditions remain shared.

The readiness amendment at `2026-11-13T17:47:51.551317+00:00` predates final launch at `2026-11-13T17:47:59.444292+00:00` and is hash-bound in the final-start marker. It explicitly permits unrelated user jobs/services on a shared host; only the four registered workers were allowed to run FFWB experiments. This review verifies that prior declaration and its evidence binding, not whole-machine isolation or continuous monitoring. The interval's coverage and inferential interpretation remain conditional on independent bounded pair outcomes. This result supports observed local performance against this v2 configuration; it is not an algorithm-only result, controlled-hardware result or MIT arena/Elo claim.

No controls or package smoke games were evaluated here. Their release gates remain separate. No matches were executed during this audit, and raw data/runtime files were unchanged.

Machine evidence: [outcome-audit-v5.json](../outputs/outcome-audit-v5.json), SHA256 `cf235ce1c38660b7faa5b612d45135669a6c4e32eba0eb7b08c14fea79f9912d`. It contains all input/source hashes, 200 pair W/B scores, per-color/batch records, runtime identity, findings and the complete reproducible audit program. Review created `2026-11-13T18:42:07.861233+00:00`. The prose formatting was cleaned up after the numerical audit; the embedded audit program is the exact executed source.

# V5 local validation — November 13, 2026

**V5 passed the frozen local comparison against released v2: 261 wins, 8 draws and 131 losses in 400 games, a 66.25% score.** All 400 games were retained and independently replay-audited, with zero failures. Separate regression controls passed, and the actual extracted submission launcher passed both smoke games. **Final native QA and release acceptance are pending.** MIT arena Elo remains unmeasured; the 2200–2500 target is not established by these results.

The selected configuration is `learned_600`, using the repaired experimental runtime already present before the V5 campaign:

```text
--risk-policy learned --search-ms 600 --particles 256 --worlds 6 --depth 4 --nodes 120000
```

Its `bot.py` SHA256 is `0d00f07a120166821b76a04e5ef2eb991c8197701bb4392d082ebbec5d4a85e8`. The opponent is the byte-exact v2 snapshot from commit `65fde033a2e65394a676e44969a992832ee17470`, run through `v2_bot.py --search-ms 180`. Both received 180 seconds plus 2 seconds per move, with a 1,000-ply cap. **The candidate's 600 ms internal allowance versus v2's 180 ms makes this a comparison against the released product, not a compute-matched or algorithm-only result.**

The [global design](v5-cycle-20261113/design.json), [wave plan](v5-cycle-20261113/wave-001/plan.json) and [source archive](v5-cycle-20261113/wave-001/sources.zip) were frozen before play. Four configurations received eight color-swapped seed pairs each. The best two received 32 fresh pairs each; qualification required scores above 50% in both fixed 16-pair halves and no failures. All development records remain intact:

| Configuration | Screen W/D/L, 16 games | Confirmation W/D/L, 64 games | Confirmation score |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| hypothesis, 128 particles, 4 worlds, depth 5 | 9/0/7 | Not selected | — |
| robust, 128 particles, 4 worlds, depth 5 | 11/0/5 | Not selected | — |
| bank, 256 particles, 6 worlds, depth 4 | 12/0/4 | 41/3/20 | 66.40625% |
| learned, 256 particles, 6 worlds, depth 4 | 12/1/3 | 53/1/10 | 83.59375% |

All four used 600 ms and 120,000 nodes. Learned's confirmation halves scored 84.375% and 82.8125%; bank's scored 67.1875% and 65.625%. The frozen rule selected learned before the final. These 192 development games are selection evidence, not part of the final strength estimate.

The [complete final](v5-cycle-20261113/wave-001/final-learned_600/suite.json) used 200 new color-swapped pairs in four 100-game batches, with seed bases 1793702664, 1793712664, 1793722664 and 1793732664. All planned games completed; no score-based stopping, selected subset or retry was used.

| Candidate color | Wins | Draws | Losses | Score |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| White | 125 | 4 | 71 | 63.50% |
| Black | 136 | 4 | 60 | 69.00% |
| Total | 261 | 8 | 131 | 66.25% |

The final produced **265 points out of 400**, exceeding the frozen minimum of 244. For each bounded pair score, `Xi = (white points + black points) / 2`, the declared two-sided Hoeffding radius is `sqrt(log(2 / (0.05/3)) / (2*200)) = 0.109401688090`. The resulting interval is **55.3098%–77.1902%**, with its lower endpoint above 50%. The prospective Bonferroni allocation allowed at most three finals; only the first was needed. This interval's coverage is **conditional on independent bounded pair outcomes**. Distinct seeds, color pairing and the allocation itself do not establish independence.

The [independent outcome review](../analysis/outcome-v5-review.md) and [reproducible machine audit](outcome-audit-v5.json) recomputed results and pair scores from raw replays without trusting the stored gate. They verified all 200 pairs, the frozen arguments/interpreter, all 24 final source bindings, archived sources and exact v2 provenance. Official-rule replay reconstruction checked all 400 games and 28,675 plies, including legal moves, both observations, clocks and terminal outcomes, with zero errors or recorded failures. All 400 full move trajectories were distinct, but only five four-ply opening prefixes occurred; trajectory uniqueness is not independence. The outcome-audit SHA256 is `cf235ce1c38660b7faa5b612d45135669a6c4e32eba0eb7b08c14fea79f9912d`.

**Shared-host limitation.** Before the final, whole-machine isolation was found unavailable because unrelated jobs and services continued. The [prospective readiness amendment](v5-cycle-20261113/final-readiness.json), created at 17:47:51 UTC and bound into the 17:47:59 UTC final-start marker, permitted unrelated host work while restricting FFWB experiments to the four registered workers. Independent [SoloCo methodology review](source-review-v5-shared-host.json) accepted that narrower condition. The original stronger condition remains recorded as unsatisfied. Before/after process observations do not prove continuous isolation or pair independence; shared load can affect the implementations differently. Reported performance therefore belongs to this local shared-host setup.

Across 14,305 completed candidate responses, charged latency was p50 600.898 ms, p95 602.756 ms, p99 605.278 ms and maximum 652.933 ms. These clock deltas include IPC and scheduling, not just CPU search. The internal deadline is cooperative, not a hard real-time guarantee.

The separate [release-control plan](v5-cycle-20261113/release-controls-plan.json) and [completed report](v5-cycle-20261113/release-controls/report.json) retain all 60 games. Each opponent received ten complete color pairs with the same selected candidate, 180+2 clocks and distinct registered seeds. Each suite used two five-pair jobs under a four-worker ceiling. Every replay was reconstructed independently; all controls had zero failures.

| Regression opponent | W/D/L | Score | Required score | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Legacy v1 | 19/0/1 | 95% | 75% | Pass |
| Official baseline | 20/0/0 | 100% | 90% | Pass |
| Uniform random | 20/0/0 | 100% | 95% | Pass |

These are separate regression checks. Their 59 wins and one loss are not pooled with the v2 comparison or used for an Elo estimate.

**Correctness and review evidence.** The [host test receipt](tests-v5.json) records all 188 Python tests passing in 60.075 seconds, including selected-runtime, harness, guard and package-verifier tests, plus tests of unselected prototypes. An initial Node check failed by applying the payload bound to a mixed development-file set of 250,562 bytes. That failure remains in the receipt; its `all_passed: false` is not rewritten. The [corrected static receipt](package-static-tests-v5.json) records both checks passing after applying the unchanged 250,000-byte limit to the exact eleven-file runtime allowlist. The [final static receipt](package-static-tests-v5-final.json) records both checks passing again after the README update. The separate generated-development bound remains 200,000 bytes. No selected algorithm, model, harness or match input changed for this correction.

The original [V5 evaluator QA Fail](source-review-v5-evaluation-failed.json) remains preserved. It identified unenforced interpreter identity, missing exact wave/opponent evidence and a concurrent-invocation race. The new prospective guard checks the exact interpreter/dependency fingerprint and holds an experiment lock through delegation; seven executed guard regressions passed. The [supplemental source-only Pass](source-review-v5-evaluation-repair.json), artifact `artifact-4665fbff-f1bb-4c7a-97c9-630c29623fb1`, closed that narrow remedy. Development's earlier direct invocation was not retrospectively guarded. Guard checks are trusted-local entry checks, not continuous attestation or exclusion of arbitrary host work. Source review and host execution are distinct evidence; neither is native company-development acceptance.

**Verified delivery.** [submission-v5-final.zip](submission-v5-final.zip) is **137,624 bytes**, with **136,506 uncompressed payload bytes** across exactly eleven regular allowlisted entries. Its SHA256 is `5b190981af47c62f9cd22834eb0bffc4be06611ac43cf6d106b6db910083d99c`. The executable `run.sh` embeds the selected arguments; runtime bytes match the frozen candidate, and official upstream files retain their expected hashes. Environments, credentials and SoloCo state are excluded.

The [extracted-package verification](package-check-v5/verification.json) passed with unchanged sources, worker exit 0 and no errors. Its actual launcher completed two normal wins against legacy v1, one per color; both full replays passed auditing. These are compatibility checks, not strength evidence. Across 44 candidate responses, p95 was 601.699 ms and maximum 602.644 ms. Maximum reaped-child RSS was **52,215,808 bytes** in the fresh local worker. That high-water measurement covers both bot roles under OS descendant accounting; it is not candidate-only memory, summed concurrent memory or an arena container measurement.

**Final native QA and release acceptance: PENDING.** The completed comparison, controls, tests and package checks above do not by themselves claim that final acceptance has occurred. The acceptance owner will add the exact final review and decision here without changing the historical results.

**Preserved failures and notices.** [V3](validation-v3.md) remains a failed promotion test: 97 wins, one draw and 102 losses against v2. [V4](validation-v4.md) remains a failed selected-prefix mechanism test: both variants chose three immediately fatal actions in 90 prefixes and avoided neither original trap. Its full-game stages were not run; the documented stop deviation and unused seeds remain preserved. V5's separately frozen full-game result does not relabel those earlier tests.

The [original validation record](validation.md) documents resolution of both original SoloCo notices on November 12, without erasing their failed/cancelled jobs:

- `notice-1f3bf4fd-fe7b-426b-87c6-4a76d59f926a`: “Specialist engineer could not finish: Candidate exceeds byte limit: actual 114050, permitted 100000, excess 14050”. The supported project ceiling was raised to 250,000 bytes; the original immutable scope and spent attempt were retained.
- `notice-a6d47547-eafc-4b33-a79a-30c3fb8296b6`: “Specialist engineer could not finish: Role session cancelled; held for inspection, not automatically retried”. Process closure and resource release were confirmed; the correction was completed through the separately authorized host workflow, without claiming native acceptance of the cancelled job.
- The later `notice-98f1b24d-ae51-4cda-a1c7-4e1fa8d1ab40` records: “Specialist qa could not finish: Role session cancelled; held for inspection, not automatically retried”. This V4 model-QA assignment's closure was inspected and a replacement [scoped model review](source-review-v4-model.json) passed. The cancellation and notice remain historical evidence; this report does not claim a new notice-ledger resolution. The separate 200,000-character specialist-context limit is not the 250,000-byte project/package limit.

`bot_v5.py`, `belief_v5.py`, `threat_policy.py` and `fog_pressure.py` are additional research prototypes, excluded from the selected launcher and ZIP. Their unit tests do not establish playing strength, and none supplies the reported final result. The bundled learned model was trained on earlier V3 data, with truth used only for offline labels; the [training report](risk-model-training-v4.json) retains grouped splits, calibration limitations and numerical warnings. Runtime policy inputs remain observations, known own moves/captures and clocks.

All execution was local macOS arm64/Python 3.13.2 with chess 1.11.2 and python-chess 1.999. Official Linux amd64/Python 3.14.8 sandbox behavior and actual arena ratings remain unverified. No arena account, submission, paid compute or background automation was used. The evidence supports the observed local result against this exact v2 configuration; it does not establish 2200–2500 MIT Elo or general strongest-bot status.

rules.confirmation_gate: zero failures and score strictly above .5 in each 16-pair block and overall
rules.failed_candidate_policy: retain failed stage evidence; candidate ineligible; source drift aborts whole wave
rules.final_readiness: development stops at final_ready; explicit final command records native QA and exclusive-host readiness
rules.final_selection: highest confirmation score among qualifiers, ties by frozen candidate order
rules.final_statistical_gate: complete audited final; mean pair score minus sqrt(log(2/alpha)/(2*n)) > .5
rules.retry_policy: at most one final per wave; later frozen waves may adapt to prior results; fresh final seeds
rules.selection: highest completed screen score, ties by frozen candidate order; top two confirm
rules.stop_policy: finish every started successful stage; stop cycle at first final statistical pass; no score-based early stopping
rules.zero_failures: qualifying candidate screen, confirmation and final must all be complete and failure-free
